title: Advertising in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about advertising: how much is spent, who blocks it, who polices it and where it's no longer allowed.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are.

outro.heading: Attention is expensive.
paras: Advertisers spend more than ever, while a large share of people block ads and regulators keep adding rules. Every advert has to earn attention from an audience that is often trying to avoid it.
Today you'll argue about how a campaign should do that. Use the evidence your team brings.

questions.q: Roughly how much was spent on advertising worldwide in 2025?
questions.explain: WARC estimates $1.19 trillion for 2025. Most of the growth goes to three companies, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet, which are expected to take almost 59% of the market outside China by 2027.
questions.source: WARC global ad forecast, December 2025 (Advanced Television)

questions.q: On YouTube, many video adverts show a 'Skip' button. After how many seconds can viewers usually skip?
questions.explain: Skippable in-stream ads can be skipped after 5 seconds, and on view-based bidding advertisers pay only if people watch 30 seconds or click. So the first five seconds have to do most of the work: brand, hook and reason to stay.
questions.source: Google Ads Help, About video ad formats

questions.q: What share of internet users worldwide use an ad blocker at least some of the time?
questions.explain: About 29.5% of internet users block ads, according to GWI data for Q2 2025. In Germany it's 31.5% and in the UK about 28.5%. Blocking is now a normal habit, not something only tech fans do.
questions.source: GWI, Q2 2025 data, via DataReportal (Backlinko summary, 2025)

questions.q: In 2024 the UK's Advertising Standards Authority got 33,903 ads changed or withdrawn. What share did it find with its own AI monitoring, rather than through public complaints?
questions.explain: The ASA's Active Ad Monitoring system scanned about 28 million online ads in 2024 and found 94% of the problem ads. The public still sent 37,284 complaints, most of them about online ads.

questions.q: Since January 2026, adverts for less healthy food and drink have been banned on UK TV before what time?
questions.sub: and no paid online ads at all
questions.explain: Since 5 January 2026, these ads can't run on UK TV between 5.30am and 9pm, and can't appear in paid-for online advertising at any time. The aim is to cut children's exposure to junk food marketing.

questions.q: In 2024 Edinburgh banned high-carbon adverts on council-owned advertising sites. Which cars may still be advertised there?
options: Any car with a top safety rating
questions.explain: Adverts for petrol, diesel, hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars are banned, along with airlines, cruises and fossil fuel firms. Battery-electric and hydrogen cars are allowed, but not SUVs.
questions.source: Air Quality News; PA Media, May 2024

questions.q: What share of new cars registered in the EU in 2025 were fully battery-electric?
questions.explain: Battery-electric cars took 17.4% of the EU market in 2025. Hybrids sold even more, and petrol and diesel cars together still had over a third of the market.

questions.q: UK advertisers spend the most in the run-up to Christmas. How much was forecast for October to December 2025?
questions.explain: The Advertising Association and WARC forecast £12.0 billion for the 'golden quarter', 7.3% more than a year before. That's about £130 million a day.
questions.source: Advertising Association / WARC Expenditure Report, October 2025 (Marketing Week)
